segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ יָשְׁנוּ מִקְצָתָן — יֹאכֵלוּ. כּוּלָּן — לֹא יֹאכֵלוּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «If some of» the participants at the seder «fell asleep,» thereby interrupting their meal, «they» may «eat» from the Paschal lamb when they awake. If the «entire» company fell asleep, «they» may «not eat» any more. If they all fall asleep, this is considered a complete interruption, and if they were to resume their meal it would be akin to eating the offering in two different places.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נִתְנַמְנְמוּ — יֹאכֵלוּ, נִרְדְּמוּ — לֹא יֹאכֵלוּ. הַפֶּסַח אַחַר חֲצוֹת מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם. הַפִּגּוּל וְהַנּוֹתָר מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yosei says:» If «they dozed they» may «eat» from the Paschal lamb when they awake, but if «they fell» fast «asleep they» may «not eat» from it. The Sages further said: «The Paschal lamb after midnight renders one’s hands ritually impure,» as it becomes notar, an offering that remained after the time when they may be eaten has expired; and the Sages ruled that both «piggul,» offerings that were invalidated due to inappropriate intent while being sacrificed, «and notar render one’s hands ritually impure.»
